label: Transit access
hint: Lines, modes and frequency within a 12 min walk
info: How many ways out you have on foot. Counts {modeList} lines within 1,000 m (a 12 minute walk), weighted by weekday frequency (regional counts most, then S/U, then tram) and by distance: full weight up to 250 m, fading to nothing at 1,000 m. A bonus for every extra transit type. Buses are not counted. 0 means no such stop within 1,000 m. Many lines beat one frequent line. Source: {timetable}.
note: Lines within 1 km, weighted by frequency, type and distance.

label: Commute Time
hint: Weighted time to your pinned places
info: Door-to-door travel time from a spot to each of your commute places, combined by the importance you set. The faster the better: 100 points at 10 min, 50 at 45 min, 0 at 90 min. Timetable of the next weekday, arriving 09:00, walking included. Only walking and trains count: {modeList} lines. Long-distance trains (ICE, IC), buses and ferries are left out, so every trip fits a Deutschlandticket. Each transfer counts as 6 extra minutes, so direct trains win. Source: Transitous / {timetable}.

label: City centre
info: Straight-line distance to {centreWhere} ({centrePlace}).{centreExtra} Closer scores higher: 100 within 3 km, 0 from 16 km. This keeps the ranking from favouring cheap, green outskirts and points to the in-between spots, close enough to the city yet not in its middle.

label: Rent Price
hint: Average rent from the prices people report
info: Average rent, from prices people put on the map as euros per m² (click the map, enter a price from a source you trust). Everyone sees the same prices. A price counts for its whole area: {zoneKinds}. Several reports in one area are averaged. The score uses the price per m², so the size of your flat never changes the ranking; the size you expect (Profile tab) only turns it into the monthly rent shown. To stay fair, rent only counts in the overall score once EVERY area has a price; until then the layer shows which areas still need one.{rentGaps} Cheaper is better: 100 points at {scaleFrom} €/m² or less, 0 at {scaleTo} €/m² or more.

label: Perceived safety at night
hint: Residents who feel safe after dark where they live

label: Calmness
hint: Average traffic noise at the facades (dB Lden)

label: Building Age
hint: Average year built, newer is better

label: Amenities
info: Daily needs within 800 m: supermarkets, bakeries, pharmacies, cafés, restaurants, doctors, post office, library, kindergartens. Each category is capped so one type cannot dominate. Source: OpenStreetMap, so it reflects how well the area is mapped.
note: Daily-needs places within 800 m, each type capped.

label: Restaurants
hint: How many restaurants, and how good
info: Restaurants within 600 m (OpenStreetMap), multiplied by how well rated the best restaurants of the area are: the average rating of the 20 most popular ones, from the ratings service chosen when the data was built (named in Sources). Many places of high quality score most; a few average places score little. The ratings were fetched once and only this per-area average is kept. Zero means no restaurant mapped nearby.
note: Restaurants within 600 m, times how well rated the area’s best ones are.

label: Landmarks
info: How close the famous places are, the landmark pins of the map. Each counts fully within 250 m and fades to nothing at 1,000 m, like the transit stops; the big names (Brandenburger Tor, Fernsehturm, Sanssouci ...) count most, local ones less. 0 means no landmark within 1,000 m, which is the case for most of the outskirts. Source: Wikipedia positions of a hand-picked list.
note: Landmarks within 1 km, fading with distance.

label: Green space
info: Share of the 500 m circle around the hex centre covered by parks, forest, meadows, gardens, cemeteries and water (OpenStreetMap). Street trees are not counted. Map overlay only, not part of the overall score.
note: Share of the 500 m around a spot that is green or water.
